rca of the issue: Root cause: package.json pinned react-day-picker@8.10.1, which declares peer deps `react ^16-18` and `date-fns ^2.28.0 || ^3.0.0`. But the app uses react@19.0.0 and date-fns@4.1.0, producing two simultaneous ERESOLVE errors on any fresh `npm install`. Fix: bumped react-day-picker to 9.14.0 (which accepts React 19 and consumes date-fns v4 as a DIRECT dependency instead of a peer). Migrated the sole consumer (frontend/src/components/ui/calendar.jsx) from v8's `IconLeft`/`IconRight` + old classNames to v9's `Chevron` slot + new classNames (month_caption, button_previous, button_next, day_button, weekdays, weekday, week, month_grid, selected, today, outside, range_middle, range_start, range_end, hidden, disabled). No other package versions touched. package-lock.json regenerated. Verification confirmed on clean copy: install + build + peer-check + pytest all green.
